segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip slowly took off his houndstooth detective cap, holding it in his paws. His yellow eyes were wide with wonder as he looked up at you.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Good heavens,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip whispered softly, his pompous accent completely gone.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I thought... I thought I was the one rescuing you. But all along... you're the one who was meant to save us.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: We're a team, Pip,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, looking down at the little fox.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: We wouldn't have made it past the snowbank without you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip’s ears twitched with pride. He quickly jammed his hat back onto his head, cleared his throat, and puffed out his chest:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem! Well! Naturally! A brilliant partnership between legendary intuition and tactical genius! Precisely as I calculated!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby chuckled—a warm, gravelly sound—and turned back to his workbench.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With both hands, he unrolled a colossal, glowing parchment blueprint across the iron table, weighing down the corners with two brass gears.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The blueprint showed the towering, intricate anatomy of the Grand Christmas Clock: thousands of interlocking wheels, spinning balance springs, and a colossal crystal core at the very center.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Now,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby said, his voice turning sharp and focused.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Here is what my old master has done. Look at the central escapement.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You lean over the parchment. Immediately, your eyes zero in on the center of the diagram. While Pip and Barnaby squint at the tiny mechanical notes, you intuitively trace the flow of energy through the brass pipes.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: The pendulum,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, pointing your finger at a massive gear in the center.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: It’s missing its teeth on the right side.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby’s white eyebrows shot up in astonishment.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Great gears and gaskets... you saw it in five seconds. It took me three months to find that fault.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby pointed a leather-gloved finger at the missing gear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Clockmaker didn't destroy the Great Clock. He removed the Forward Escapement Gear—the Master Cog that allows time to tick into tomorrow. He replaced it with an Inverted Spiral that forces the clock to turn backward. That’s why the hours are counting down: thirteen, twelve, eleven...

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby looked at you with grim urgency.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If that clock reaches zero before Christmas Day, the reverse loop locks forever. Yesterday will vanish. And the world will never see tomorrow again.
